test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 06 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. He surveyed the way over to the terrace from which the archers had fired.

A. Going to the side of the bridge, he judged distances and how difficult it would be to reach that terrace, drew the Blades of Athena, and then leaped into space.

B. The archers had to be guarding something important.

C. That provided him as good a direction to explore as any.

D. And if he approached cautiously enough, he might find a way to declare his intentions of speaking with the Sisters of Fate so he would not have to fight his way through a phalanx of other guards.

S2. The blades dug into the ornate stonework facing the palace wall.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph describes a character's tactical decision-making and physical action as he moves toward a specific goal.
 
• **Sentence C is the first sentence** following S1 because it directly references the "direction" established by the terrace mentioned in the opening sentence:
 
 
• "That provided him as good a direction to explore as any."
 
 
 
• **Sentence B follows** as it provides the logical reasoning for why that direction is worth exploring, linking the presence of archers to something valuable:
 
 
• "The archers had to be guarding something important."
 
 
 
• **Sentence D is the third sentence** because it elaborates on his plan and specific objective (reaching the Sisters of Fate) while maintaining caution:
 
 
• "And if he approached cautiously enough, he might find a way to declare his intentions of speaking with the Sisters of Fate..."
 
 
 
• **Sentence A is the fourth** as it transitions from mental planning to physical execution, describing the leap that leads directly into the final sentence S2:
 
 
• "Going to the side of the bridge, he judged distances... drew the Blades of Athena, and then leaped into space."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **CBDA**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"He surveyed the way over to the terrace from which the archers had fired. That provided him as good a direction to explore as any. The archers had to be guarding something important. And if he approached cautiously enough, he might find a way to declare his intentions of speaking with the Sisters of Fate so he would not have to fight his way through a phalanx of other guards. Going to the side of the bridge, he judged distances and how difficult it would be to reach that terrace, drew the Blades of Athena, and then leaped into space. The blades dug into the ornate stonework facing the palace wall."
